title: Folklore Conjecture (polynomial bound for linear hypergraphs)
statement_text: $r(F, K_{n}^{(3)})$ is at most polynomial in $n$ for any linear $3$-graph $F$.
context_text: This unpublished folklore conjecture was circulating in the Ramsey theory community and was also a special case of a broader unpublished conjecture about $123$-inducible $3$-graphs. Theorem 1.4 disproves it by constructing a linear $3$-graph $H$ for which $r(H, K_{n}^{(3)})$ is superpolynomial in $n$, yielding the first separation between $r(H, K_{n}^{(3)})$ and $r(H, K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})$ for linear $H$.
paper_contribution: Disproves the conjecture (Theorem 1.4) by exhibiting a linear $3$-graph $H$ for which $r(H, K_{n}^{(3)})$ is superpolynomial in $n$, providing the first separation between $r(H,K_{n}^{(3)})$ and $r(H,K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})$ for linear $H$.
notes: Explicitly called 'a folklore conjecture in the area' in the abstract; its precise statement is reconstructed from the discussion surrounding Conjecture 4.7.

title: Conjecture 4.1
statement_text: There exists an absolute constant $a>0$ such that, for all $3$-graphs $G$ and $H$, $r^{p}(G,H)\geq r(G,H)^{a}$ whenever $p>r(G,H)^{o(1)}$.
context_text: A $3$-graph is a $3$-uniform hypergraph; $K_N^{(3)}$ is the complete $3$-graph on $N$ vertices and $K_{n,n,n}^{(3)}$ the complete $3$-partite $3$-graph with three parts of size $n$. The Ramsey number $r(G,H)$ is the smallest $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(3)}$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$; subscripts in $O_H$, $\Theta_H$, $\Omega_s$ mean that the implied constants depend on $H$ or $s$. A (3-uniform) pair construction on vertex set $[N]$ is a red/blue coloring $\chi_{f,g}$ of $K_N^{(3)}$ obtained from two functions $f:\binom{[N]}{2}\to[p]$ and $g:[p]^3\to\{\text{red},\text{blue}\}$ by setting $\chi_{f,g}(\{i,j,k\})=g(f(i,j),f(j,k),f(k,i))$ for $i<j<k$; the parameter $p$ is its complexity. Then $r^p(G,H)$ is the smallest $n$ such that every pair construction on $K_n^{(3)}$ of complexity at most $p$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$. Stepping-up constructions (where $f(i,j)$ is the index of the most significant binary digit in which $i$ and $j$ differ, complexity typically $O(\log N)$) and inducibility constructions (random $f$, constant complexity) are pair constructions, as are both constructions of this paper. The conjecture says that if there is a Ramsey coloring of order $N$, then there is one of order $N^{\Omega(1)}$ of much smaller complexity, which would explain the prevalence of such constructions and might shed light on the growth rates of $r(H,K_n^{(3)})$. The authors also show that polylogarithmic complexity does not suffice in general: $r^p(K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})\le 2^{O(n\log p)}$, so complexity $2^{\Omega(n)}$ is needed to reach $r(K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})^{\Omega(1)}$.

title: Conjecture 4.3
context_text: A $3$-graph is a $3$-uniform hypergraph; $K_N^{(3)}$ is the complete $3$-graph on $N$ vertices and $K_{n,n,n}^{(3)}$ the complete $3$-partite $3$-graph with three parts of size $n$. The Ramsey number $r(G,H)$ is the smallest $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(3)}$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$; subscripts in $O_H$, $\Theta_H$, $\Omega_s$ mean that the implied constants depend on $H$ or $s$. Fox and He showed $r(H,K_n^{(3)})=2^{\Theta_H(n\log n)}$ when $H$ is the link of an odd cycle (the link of a graph $G$ is the $3$-graph on $V(G)\cup\{u\}$, $u$ a new vertex, with edges $e\cup\{u\}$ for $e\in E(G)$), and this paper extends the $2^{\Omega_H(n\log n)}$ lower bound to many more $3$-graphs (including tight cycles of length not divisible by 3), with a matching upper bound for many of them. Strangely, no $3$-graph $H$ with $r(H,K_n^{(3)})=2^{\Theta_H(n)}$ is known. Call $H$ $123$-inducible if there is an ordering of $V(H)$ and a labelling of the pairs covered by edges of $H$ with $1,2,3$ such that for every edge $uvw$ with $u<v<w$, $uv$ is labelled 1, $vw$ is labelled 2 and $uw$ is labelled 3; Erdős and Hajnal proved that if $H$ is not $123$-inducible then $r(H,K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})\ge 2^{\Omega_H(n)}$. The authors construct (by gluing the links of two paths on 12 vertices along some vertices without sharing edges) a $3$-graph $H$ that is not $123$-inducible, so $r(H,K_n^{(3)})\ge 2^{\Omega_H(n)}$, but to which their $2^{\Omega(n\log n)}$ lower bound does not apply; they suggest it as a promising candidate. For families the rate is attainable: for the family of links of nonbipartite graphs, the Ramsey number is $2^{\Theta(n)}$.

title: Conjecture 4.6
statement_text: For every $c>0$, there exists $s$ such that $r(K_{s}^{(3)},K_{n}^{(3)})\geq 2^{\Omega_{s}(n^{c})}$.
context_text: A $3$-graph is a $3$-uniform hypergraph; $K_N^{(3)}$ is the complete $3$-graph on $N$ vertices and $K_{n,n,n}^{(3)}$ the complete $3$-partite $3$-graph with three parts of size $n$. The Ramsey number $r(G,H)$ is the smallest $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(3)}$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$; subscripts in $O_H$, $\Theta_H$, $\Omega_s$ mean that the implied constants depend on $H$ or $s$. For fixed $s$, Conlon, Fox and Sudakov showed $2^{cn\log n}\le r(K_s^{(3)},K_n^{(3)})\le 2^{Cn^{s-2}\log n}$. The outstanding question on off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers is whether some fixed $3$-graph $H$ has $r(H,K_n^{(3)})\ge 2^{\omega(n\log n)}$; the authors believe this already holds for $H=K_4^{(3)}$ but their methods do not suffice, and they conjecture the much stronger statement here. They note that it fails with $K_{n,n,n}^{(3)}$ in place of $K_n^{(3)}$, since $r(H,K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})\le 2^{O_H(n^2)}$ for every $H$ (and even $2^{O_H(n^{2-\epsilon})}$ for some $\epsilon>0$ depending on $H$). They also ask which growth rates are possible for fixed $H$ (e.g. $2^{\Theta_H(\sqrt n)}$ or $2^{\Theta_H(n\log\log n)}$), noting that for the family of links of nonbipartite graphs the rate $2^{\Theta(n)}$ occurs.

title: Conjecture 4.7
statement_text: There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that $r(F,K_{n}^{(3)})\leq 2^{O_{F}(n^{C})}$ for every fixed linear $3$-graph $F$.
context_text: A $3$-graph is a $3$-uniform hypergraph; $K_N^{(3)}$ is the complete $3$-graph on $N$ vertices and $K_{n,n,n}^{(3)}$ the complete $3$-partite $3$-graph with three parts of size $n$. The Ramsey number $r(G,H)$ is the smallest $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(3)}$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$; subscripts in $O_H$, $\Theta_H$, $\Omega_s$ mean that the implied constants depend on $H$ or $s$. A $3$-graph is linear if any two of its edges share at most one vertex. It was a folklore conjecture that $r(F,K_n^{(3)})$ is polynomial in $n$ for every linear $F$ (it is known that $r(F,K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})$ is polynomial for linear $F$, by Fox and He). The authors disprove it: for all large $k$ there is a linear $3$-graph $F$ on $k$ vertices with $r(F,K_n^{(3)})>2^{c(\log n)^{\sqrt{k}/(128\log^5 k)}}$, $c>0$ depending on $k$. For linear $F$ on $s$ vertices, the arguments of Conlon, Fox and Sudakov give $r(F,K_n^{(3)})\le 2^{n^{s-\Omega(s^{1/2})}}$, and the authors believe the much stronger subexponential bound conjectured here may be true. They mention possible strengthenings, with $n^C$ replaced by $n^{o(1)}$, or with linear $3$-graphs replaced by $123$-inducible ones ($H$ is $123$-inducible if there is an ordering of $V(H)$ and a labelling by $1,2,3$ of the pairs covered by edges such that every edge $uvw$, $u<v<w$, has $uv,vw,uw$ labelled $1,2,3$ respectively), but are less certain about these.

title: Informal conjecture on tripartite off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
statement_text: It may be the case that $r(H,K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})\leq 2^{O_{H}(n\log n)}$ for all $H$.
context_text: A $3$-graph is a $3$-uniform hypergraph; $K_N^{(3)}$ is the complete $3$-graph on $N$ vertices and $K_{n,n,n}^{(3)}$ the complete $3$-partite $3$-graph with three parts of size $n$. The Ramsey number $r(G,H)$ is the smallest $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of $K_N^{(3)}$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$; subscripts in $O_H$, $\Theta_H$, $\Omega_s$ mean that the implied constants depend on $H$ or $s$. It is easy to see that $r(H,K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})\le 2^{O_H(n^2)}$ for every $3$-graph $H$, and using methods of Conlon, Fox and Sudakov one can show that for every $H$ there is $\epsilon>0$ with $r(H,K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})\le 2^{O_H(n^{2-\epsilon})}$. On the other hand the authors prove $r(H,K_{n,n,n}^{(3)})\ge 2^{\Omega_H(n\log n)}$ for many $H$ (e.g. links of odd cycles and tight cycles of length not divisible by 3), tight in several cases. They suspect that $2^{O_H(n\log n)}$ is the truth for all $H$, which would go some way towards explaining why the threshold $2^{\Theta(n\log n)}$ is so hard to surpass in lower-bound constructions for $r(H,K_n^{(3)})$.
notes: Introduced with 'We suspect that it may even be the case' in the discussion following Conjecture 4.6.
